statement: What waits for bytes the Host cannot read is only what comes from those bytes; a dispute start, a counter and the windows are never held. A dispute op whose transaction the node will not give (an input or a trace that fails, null for a transaction it does not know) cannot be read yet (R-WATCH-CALLDATA). (1) A START is told at once as its log has it: the window, the nonce, the opening proof's hash and the secrets in its arguments are all in the log, so the Entity hears a dispute against it, and every event that opens or closes its response window, in time (the counter registers only if the hearing delay plus lag is under the window, and with a transient revert of the ask under the window less two lags: the model of the spec compare of #171). Only its body comes from the bytes: the start waits in the carry's `reading`, is told again with the body when the bytes come (the Entity takes the body of the dispute it holds only if it hashes to the logged body hash and it has none), and is told `j_start_unread` once a delivery's last block is past the window's end (the chain's second, never a count of ticks). A start of the Entity's own needs no bytes and none is asked. (2) A FINALIZE holds back the events of its own Account from its first event on, in the chain's order (a finalize's first event is the epoch advance it made): `j_dispute_over` dissolves the Account's holds and fails the locks the Entity forwarded to that peer back upstream (entity/frame.ts `finalized`), so a secret in the finalize's arguments must be heard first (R-HOLD-DISSOLVE), and a later event of the Account (the epoch it moved to) cannot be told ahead of the advance (R-HEIGHT-ORDER, the Entity drops a dispute of another epoch). Every other Account's events and every SecretRevealed go on at once. Holding a finalize costs nothing on that Account: it takes no new frame (a hold of it dissolves at the finalize, and a start in the epoch after has no proof of the Entity's to be countered by, since it signed none while behind). (3) THE DECISION IS PER ACCOUNT of the transaction: one transaction may carry the ops of several Accounts (a multicall), a stranger's among them, and each event of it waits or is given up for its own Account at its own bound; a stranger's op is not read at all, so it never shortens the wait of the Entity's. (4) THE RECORD. The Entity is told `j_behind {peer, from}` when the Host first owes it events of an Account (held events, or a start read pending; the first block) and `j_behind_over {peer}` when it owes none, the latter only once the delivery's height reaches the Entity's view; the chain facts keep the first block (`behind`). A restart begins reading at `min(view, min(behind) - 1)`, so what was owed is read again; every J event is idempotent. (5) WHILE BEHIND an Account is quiet (`quiet`): the Entity signs nothing new on it and refuses its peer's frames as frozen, forwards no lock to that peer (the lock that came is given up upstream), and never co-signs an expiry of the inbound hold of a hash it forwarded to that peer (a `reveal_unknown` refusal, which can pass). A blind Entity (R-WATCH-CALLDATA, `j_blind`) forwards no lock and co-signs no expiry at all. (6) THE WAIT for a finalize is counted in chain time: at most one try per head block (a head already asked is not asked again), the first fault a head gives counts whatever it was, and none ends the wait by its own count while a forward depends on it. It ends at one of two bounds, per event. (a) The Entity has outstanding forwards to the Account's peer: when the view a delivery reaches is at least `lastHeard(peer)`, the least over its locked paybook entries to that peer of (the inbound hold's deadline - lag). The hub must answer upstream `lag` blocks before the inbound deadline and the upstream's view is at most `lag` ahead (R-HTLC-CLOCK), so a secret heard at a view up to that can be passed up in time and one view later cannot (the model of the spec compare: heard at g is safe). (b) No forward depends on it: FEW_TRIES (3) tries, one per head block. Past either the finalize is told `j_finalize_unread`, loudly, and the Account goes on. The bound (a) is later than the onward form (onward deadline - (lag + depth + 1)) by hop + depth + 1 blocks: it never gives up while the hub could still claim, and since a start is never held and the Account takes nothing new meanwhile, what the extra wait costs is only that the finalize's own events arrive later (decision of the coordinator 10-03 00:54, final). Owed: S9b on the real chain, where the hub claims with a give-up of deadline + slack - lag - depth, which needs slack >= depth (freeze-followups reserve rows); the freeze above is Entity-side only.
source: coordinator relays 10-02 23:50, 10-03 00:40, 00:51 (spec compare of #171: boundary, B9 model) and 00:54; Review A B8, B9, B10 on #171; builder 10-03

layers.arrival: n/a: the Arrival page has no chain events
layers.quint: n/a: the Quint models have the chain's cells; which secrets the watcher reads is a Host rule
layers.contract: n/a: the contract's applyPayment decides what the arguments pay; the e2e dispute-clause step reads the watcher against it

killers.name: R-WATCH-STALL the earliest block an Account was held from stands until it is over
R-WATCH-STALL a hub waits on the peer it forwarded to until the inbound deadline less the lag
R-WATCH-STALL a tx the provider refuses holds its Account only; the Entity is told it is behind
R-WATCH-STALL a tx the provider keeps refusing is waited on FEW_TRIES blocks, then told unread
R-WATCH-STALL a restart begins before the block its Account was held back from
R-WATCH-STALL a stalled tx holds back its own Account only: secrets and other Accounts go on
R-WATCH-STALL the held events follow the tx once it is given: secrets first
R-WATCH-STALL an input the node cannot give holds its Account from the finalize's advance on
R-WATCH-STALL a tx the node fails is tried once per head block, not once per poll
R-WATCH-STALL with no lock on it a tx the node fails gets FEW_TRIES blocks, then is unread
R-WATCH-STALL the Entity is told an Account is behind once, and over only from the view it is at
R-WATCH-STALL a restart begins before the earliest block the Entity was told is held back
R-WATCH-STALL a finalize the Host cannot read holds its Account from the advance it made, no other
R-WATCH-STALL with nothing stalled everything is told; a tx no event names holds nothing
R-WATCH-STALL a finalize begins at the advance it made; an earlier advance is not its own
R-WATCH-STALL what the loop waits on the Entity for: the last heard of each peer, and who is behind
R-WATCH-STALL a stall is told once, and again only when the call that fails is another
R-WATCH-STALL a trace asked at a head and refused is not asked again at that head
R-WATCH-STALL the Entity keeps the record per Account, through other news, until over
R-WATCH-STALL an Account the Host still owes events of signs nothing new, until told over
R-WATCH-STALL a dispute told without its body takes the body when it is told again with it
R-WATCH-STALL a hub forwards no lock to a peer whose events the Host still owes it
R-WATCH-STALL an expiry of the lock a hub forwarded to a peer it is behind on is not co-signed
R-WATCH-STALL a node with a forward to the peer waits past FEW_TRIES, until its lock's last view
R-WATCH-STALL an Account stays behind after a restart until a delivery reaches the WAL's view
R-WATCH-STALL a tx the node fails with a forward on it is waited on until lastHeard
R-WATCH-STALL a start behind a tx the node always fails is told at once, window and secret in it
R-WATCH-STALL a start told without its body is told again with it once the bytes come
R-WATCH-STALL a start the bytes never come for is told unread once its window has passed
R-WATCH-STALL a stranger's finalize ahead of the Entity's in one tx does not shorten the wait
R-WATCH-STALL one tx over two Accounts is given up for each at its own lastHeard
R-WATCH-STALL a start the Host cannot read holds nothing: its Account's events go on
R-WATCH-STALL a body the chain did not log the hash of is not taken, with or without one held
